newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Telekom says seeking more Africa deals.
newsitem.headline: Telekom says seeking more Africa deals.

text.p: Telekom Malaysia Bhd said on Tuesday it was in talks with more African countries for possible telecommunications ventures.
Telekom is currently a part of a U.S.-Malaysian consortium acquiring a stake in South Africa's telecommunications utility Telkom.

When asked whether Telekom was in discussions with the governments of Mozambique, Kenya or Zimbabwe, for a possible equity participation in their state-run telecommunications utlities, Telekom Malaysia's chief executive officer Mohamed Said Mohamed Ali said: "One or two of them, not all."

"We have been in contact with governments, but it would not be fair to commit them to say that the shares in their telecom companies will be given to us," said Mohamed Said. He declined to be more specific.
Daim Zainuddin, the government's economic adviser, has discussed the possibility of investing in other African countries after a recent trip to the continent, Mohamed Said told reporters.
"Tun Daim has spoken to us about other investment opportunities in Africa," Mohamed Said told reporters.
